subject: pe

moments.title: Yerkes-Dodson law
moments.body: Yerkes and Dodson's experiments on mice show that performance increases with arousal up to a point, then declines — the 'inverted-U'. Optimal arousal level depends on task complexity (simple tasks tolerate higher arousal). The law becomes a foundational sport-psychology concept.
moments.takeaway: An animal-learning experiment from 1908 organised sport psychology's first century — and is increasingly contested as an oversimplification.

moments.title: Csíkszentmihályi's flow
moments.body: Csíkszentmihályi publishes 'Beyond Boredom and Anxiety', introducing 'flow' — an optimal psychological state where challenge matches skill and self-consciousness disappears. The concept later spreads via 'Flow: The Psychology of Optimal Experience' (1990). Athletes describe flow as 'the zone'.
moments.takeaway: A Hungarian-American psychologist's interview research with chess players, climbers and surgeons named an experience athletes had long described.

now.title: Sport psychology today
now.body: Cognitive-behavioural techniques, mindfulness (MAC — Mindfulness, Acceptance, Commitment), self-talk, imagery and arousal regulation are standard practice. Bandura's self-efficacy theory (1977) and Deci-Ryan self-determination theory (1985) remain widely applied.
now.open_questions: How can performance psychology coexist with mental health support? The two are increasingly intertwined.

reflection: Csíkszentmihályi escaped post-war Hungary as a teenager. The psychology of optimal experience came partly from a refugee thinking about what made life worth living.
